label: Consanguineous marriage rate
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = a curated table of published consanguinity-prevalence readings (102 rows, 69 countries, 1943-2021, one citation per row — the consang.net global tables of A.H. Bittles' compilation carrying the national surveys and dispensation registries, plus the DHS final reports and journal studies verified directly: PDHS 2017-18 Table 4.5, El-Mouzan 2008, Saadat 2004, Ben Halim 2012, Kalam 2024, Kaplan 2016). Reliability is MIXED BY NATURE and documented per row: the European registry belt (dispensation and civil registration, N up to 1.4 million) is high; the survey belt is moderate (national samples N 1,500-306,000); the subnational and community-scope readings (entered only where no national print exists) are the table's honest frontier, each carrying its scope in definition_note. No witness tier exists (no machine-readable door carries the series — the gate finding).
license: Facts with citation (small extracts, clearly attributed) — see docs/licenses.md and catalog/curated/README.md.
notes:
THE THIRTEENTH INDICATOR, THE BACKLOG'S HEAD (v17). The corpus's #6 (34 citations, 10 books) and the one that was already waiting at v16 with its gate satisfied: consanguineous marriage is Todd's anthropological signature variable — the family-systems map's own metric (La troisième planète's world scale 0-60%, L'enfance du monde's Iran, Le Destin des immigrés' 16-citation cross-community table, Après l'Empire's early-1990s DHS reading "Sudan 57% to Turkey 15%", Qui est Charlie ?'s Maghreb ~25-35% c.2000).
THE TABLE'S SHAPE: one row per (country, study year), the value = the study's printed overall consanguineous-marriage rate in percent over the union types THAT study counts (the types ride every note: most count D1C,1C,11/2C,2C; Bahrain 2009 counts first cousins only — the perimeter is the note's job, the number is never converted). YEAR CONVENTION: the END year of the printed measurement period ('1956/57' -> 1957); the publication year where the compilation prints no period (El-Alfi 1969 -> 1969); the decade's end for a fuzzy '1970s' (1979) — the source's own period string rides every note.
THE THREE BELTS the table carries: (1) the EUROPEAN REGISTRY BELT (France 0.8 in 1958 over 510,000 dispensations, Norway's three registry vintages 0.6 -> 0.7 -> 0.1 over up to 1.4 million marriages, Spain 4.1, Italy 0.5/1.1, the two Masterson island readings Ireland 0.5 / Northern Ireland-as-UK 0.4) — the sub-1% exogamous North Todd's L'invention de l'Europe reads; (2) the LATIN DISPENSATION BELT (Freire-Maia's 1956/57 cycle across the Americas, the later Orioli/Liascovich/Castilla vintages) — Brazil 4.8 -> 1.1 -> 1.3, the Andean prints; (3) THE MUSLIM-WORLD SURVEY BELT (the corpus's heart: Pakistan's four DHS vintages 61.2 -> 60.5 -> 56.4 -> 63.9, Iran 38.6 over 306,343 couples, Saudi Arabia 56.0 national, Iraq 33.0, Jordan 39.7, Kuwait 38.4 -> 34.3, the Maghreb trio Algeria 22.6 / Morocco 19.9 / Tunisia 29.8, Turkey's four vintages 21.2 -> 18.5, Israel's Arab community 34.2 -> 22.9, Palestine's two 29.2 -> 27.7, Sudan's Khartoum 52.0) — the 20-65% belt La troisième planète's scale was built for.
THE CURATION GATE (ADR-0007, all three conditions): (a) the todd_ref demands it — 34 citations across 10 books, the heaviest concentration in Le Destin des immigrés (16); (b) the distortion is the ABSENCE — no door carries the series at all (probed live, the v16 record); (c) every row carries its citation — enforced mechanically by the connector. The rows are READ from saved evidence files (the v16 fixture lesson applied: the compilation's prints via the probe parser, the journal and DHS values via the collected abstracts and report texts — never typed from memory).
HONEST SCOPE LIMITS: the table is a SPARSE panel, not an annual series — a country rides the vintages its literature prints (Norway 3, Pakistan 4, Brazil 3; most countries 1-2 readings), which is the honest shape of this metric everywhere. Subnational and community-scope readings enter ONLY where no national print exists (each flagged SUBNATIONAL in its note with the alternative prints documented); the two Israels are the Arab community's own national surveys (the scope is the study's, the note says so). Todd's own 19th-century France and interwar Europe live in his books' tables — no citable machine print is in hand, so the table starts 1943 (the Spanish dispensation window 1940/43); the French INSEE census instrument (1975-1982 decline) is likewise a different instrument, not entered (documented on the France row). Todd's Sudan 57% (Après l'Empire's DHS-table citation) vs the entered Khartoum 52.0 — the divergence is documented on the Sudan row, as-reported on both ends.
